preamble: Vocalization of a velar stop to the palatal glide [j], usually via a fricative stage ([k] > [x] or [ɣ] > [j]). In Western Romance the first element of the Latin cluster -ct- became a yod (factum > Portuguese feito); Old Spanish shared the stage *feito before yod + t fused into the affricate of hecho. In French, intervocalic k before a voiced and weakened to yod (pacāre > payer), and in Danish postvocalic Old Norse k lenited to [j] in the pronouns mig, dig, sig. The Brittonic -ct- > -iθ development passed through a fricative *x and is filed under x → j.

examples.note: Latin -ct- > -it-; the yod is preserved (European Portuguese /ˈfɐj.tu/). Spanish carried the same stage further to hecho [ˈetʃo].
Inherited through Old Galician-Portuguese noite; Galician keeps the same form.
Intervocalic k before a voiced and spirantized, ending as the glide written y.
Postvocalic k lenited via [ɣ] to the glide [j]; likewise dig /dɑj/ 'you (obj.)'.

sources: Alkire, T., & Rosen, C. (2010). Romance Languages: A Historical Introduction. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511845192
